locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code encrypts ticket data at rest? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: The IV in FieldCipher.encrypt comes from a hash of ticketId, so every encryption for the same ticket under the same key uses the same GCM nonce. create encrypts both the customer email and the body with that nonce, and every updateBody does it again. Reusing a GCM nonce leaks the XOR of the plaintexts (anyone who knows one value, such as a customer's email, can recover the matching bytes of the body) and lets an attacker work out the GHASH key and forge tags. The IV must be random (randomBytes(12)) for each encryption.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A database administrator moves body_enc from ticket T1 into ticket T2's row. What happens when TicketRepository.get(T2) runs?
choices: It returns T1's body under T2
It returns an empty body because the keyId differs
Decryption throws, because the ticket id is used as AAD and the auth tag no longer verifies
It succeeds only if both tickets share the same status
choiceQuestions.explanation: encrypt and decrypt both call setAAD with the ticketId. The value was sealed with T1 as AAD, and get decrypts it with row.id = T2, so decipher.final() throws on tag mismatch. The keyId is the same in both rows, and status plays no part in decryption.

choiceQuestions.prompt: The KMS endpoint becomes unreachable after the service has been running and has already decrypted tickets with the current key. What happens to new get() calls for those tickets?
choices: They keep working because the key is held in the in-process cache
They fail after a 3-second timeout on every call
They hang forever because no timeout is set
They fall back to plaintext columns
choiceQuestions.explanation: KmsKeyProvider.getKey returns from this.cache before making any request, and the cache has no expiry, so keys already fetched stay usable. The 3-second timeout only applies when a key is not cached. There is a timeout, and there are no plaintext columns.

choiceQuestions.prompt: How is the connection to the KMS protected in transit?
choices: It is not; the key material is sent over plain HTTP
It uses HTTPS and trusts only certificates that chain to the configured KMS CA
It uses HTTPS but disables certificate verification
It encrypts the key material with the ticket's AAD
choiceQuestions.explanation: fetchKey uses node:https request with ca set to the KMS CA bundle. Certificate checking stays on (rejectUnauthorized defaults to true), so only a server presenting a certificate signed by that CA is accepted. Nothing turns verification off, and AAD is only used in the field cipher.
